description: Construct the applicable STDO 3.1.0-rc.1 method constraints for a pure/local Python 3.12 realization refactor under adopted DESIGN_MODULE, including its conditional ODD and UX obligations. Preserve the original family of changes to realization structure within accepted design; the request authorizes no change to public semantics or admitted domains, authority, or effects. This purpose evaluates coverage of governing method constraints before construction, not whether a particular candidate has complied with them. Concrete Product meaning, accepted design, domains, authority grants and evidence must still be acquired and applied by the task; source-complete conditional proof obligations are not claims that their future predicates already hold. Missing applicable governing law or an undecided permission actually requested remains a coverage gap. No profile is excluded merely because the implementation is pure/local. Other Product-specific or separately adopted profile law must enter through the task's exact authority packet; this index neither substitutes for it nor qualifies all STDO or every undiscovered relation. The exact source closure and independently assessed query, not this description, bound a supported coverage claim.

facts.accepted_design_available: An accepted design for the bounded task is actually available; this does not assert Prime sufficiency, candidate conformity or a completed no-delta proof.
facts.action: The authorized work class, realization_refactor. The label does not settle a discovered structural design change; that change requires owning re-entry.
facts.authority_change_authorized: Whether this request authorizes changing authority. False is a constraint on construction, not evidence that a future candidate preserved authority.
facts.effects_change_authorized: Whether this request authorizes changing externally observable effects. False is a constraint on construction, not a future verification result.
facts.explicit_failure_carrier_practical: Whether an explicit failure carrier is practical for the exact requested departure under the selected language/problem and accepted contract. Unknown practicality stays unknown; only established false can support the requested departure.
facts.failure_carrier_departure_requested: Whether this context request seeks the practicality qualification to depart from the preference for an explicit failure carrier. False leaves the qualified preference intact and grants no specific departure; no claim of candidate totality follows.
facts.grant: Existing caller work-authorization coordinate; descriptive, never a grant created by this index.
facts.language: The actual implementation language selected for this task.
facts.language_version: The language version stipulated for this task family.
facts.mutation_exception_requested: Whether this context request seeks permission for mutable semantic/source-truth carrier state. False requests ordinary immutable-carrier constraints and grants no exception; it does not forbid all imperative code or classify local scratch state as a semantic carrier. Reconstruct context if a material carrier exception is later requested.
facts.mutation_justification_present: For that same carrier exception, whether an explicit scoped justification establishes performance-critical need, host/runtime requirement, or a genuinely stateful boundary distinct from semantic truth. This is a supplied evidence premise, not a result generated by the selector.
facts.mutation_materially_necessary: For the exact requested carrier exception, whether evidence establishes material necessity under DESIGN_MODULE Immutable carriers. Convenience or the existence of legacy mutation is insufficient.
facts.profile_design_module: Whether DESIGN_MODULE is actually adopted for this task boundary. Partial adoption retains its explicitly named scope and cannot erase required design-completion evidence.
facts.profile_odd: Whether the affected boundary is governed by adopted ODD graph-execution law. Determine from actual adoption and scope, never from pure_local or the implementation language.
facts.profile_ux: Whether the affected boundary is in the Product's adopted UX scope. False alone does not establish that a UX surface is exempt from the default governing triggers.
facts.public_semantics_change_authorized: Whether this request authorizes changing public semantics or admitted domains. False forbids that change; it does not assert future equivalence.
facts.pure_local: The admitted task is a pure local transformation. This does not establish common F_D eligibility, whole-Product purity or the absence of ODD/UX scope.
facts.realizes_ux_surface: Whether this work realizes or refactors a UX surface, including a pure view/reducer/helper whose contract contributes to that surface. True includes UX default-trigger and exemption law for resolution; it does not self-adopt the profile or assert an exemption.
facts.role: Actor role bound by the actual activation; a role label creates no authority.
facts.sdlc_phase: The SDLC phase of this bounded work.
facts.source_state: Whether the exact selected governing source is current for this work; all source bytes and selected method identity are independently rehashed.
facts.target_product: Caller target Product identity, separate from the stable reusable source-corpus identity.
facts.task: Caller task identity; descriptive, not an applicability shortcut.
facts.typing_escape_excluded_from_kernel: For the exact requested escape, whether the design confines imprecision so that it never enters the semantic kernel as governing truth. This is a permission premise to be evidenced, not proof that a future candidate implements it.
facts.typing_escape_foreign_boundary: For the exact requested escape, whether the boundary is genuinely foreign/dynamic.
facts.typing_escape_narrow_justified: For the exact requested escape, whether use is narrow, explicit and justified in place.
facts.typing_escape_no_precise_local_shape: For the exact requested escape, whether local code cannot express the shape more precisely.
facts.typing_escape_requested: Whether this context request seeks permission for Any, cast or type: ignore at a specific boundary. False grants no escape and leaves the ordinary complete typing obligation intact; requery before relying on an escape.
